newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors search Yamaichi HQ - NHK.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors search Yamaichi HQ - NHK.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors began searching the headquarters of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd on Wednesday over suspicions of its involvement in a "sokaiya" racketeer payoff scandal, NHK television reported.
NHK said on Wednesday that prosecutors were searching for evindence of payoffs made to racketeers by Yamaichi.
A Yamaichi spokesman said it had not yet confirmed that the prosecutors had entered its headquarters.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun on Wednesday reported that Yamaichi and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd provided a total of 280 million yen to racketeer Ryuichi Koike in illegal deals.

The paper quoted what it said were sources close to the case as saying that Yamaichi provided Koike with 80 million yen, which it made through deals on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) in 1995, to offset stock trading losses.
Other papers also reported on Wednesday that Yamaichi provided 80 million yen to Koike.
The Nihon Keizai quoted the sources as saying Daiwa provided about 200 million yen to Koike around 1993 to offset some of his stock trading losses.

The paper said Nikko Securities Co Ltd may have also done illegal deals for Koike, a key figure in the high-profile payoff scandal which also involves Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank.

Prosecutors and Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), plan to investigate the deals at the three firms for alleged violation of securities and commercial laws, the paper said.

More than a dozen people, including top executives from DKB and Nomura, have been arrested in the affair, which coincides with the start of "Big Bang" reforms aimed at introducing more competition and global standards into Japan's long-sheltered financial sector.
The Ministry of Finance is expected to announce administrative penalties against Nomura and DKB on Wednesday.
Jiji news agency reported on Wednesday that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will also punish DKB for concealing its illegal loans to Koike during an inspection by the central bank.
